On CNBC’s “Halftime Report Final Trades,” Joseph M. Terranova, senior managing director for Virtus Investment Partners, picked Eaton Corporation plc (NYSE:ETN).

Supporting his choice, Wells Fargo analyst Stephen Tusa initiated coverage on Eaton on Sept. 25 with an Overweight rating and a price target of $503.

Stephanie Link, chief investment strategist, head of investment solutions and equity portfolio manager at Hightower Advisors, said Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) is still down 26% from its highs.

In recent news, SpaceX announced that its launch vehicle Starship (designed to carry over 100 metric tons) took flight on Monday and reached orbit on Flight 14.

Don’t forget to check out our premarket coverage here

Jason Snipe, founder and chief investment officer of Odyssey Capital Advisors, named AbbVie Inc. (NYSE:ABBV) as his final trade.

On Friday, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved AbbVie’s Juvmo (tavapadon) tablets as the first and only selective D1/D5 receptor agonist for adults with Parkinson’s disease.

Joshua Brown, co-founder and CEO of Ritholtz Wealth Management, recommended Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD).

Supporting his view, StoneX analyst Cody Acree reiterated a Buy on Advanced Micro Devices on Tuesday and maintained a $685 price target.

Price Action

  • Eaton shares gained 0.4% to close at $433.27 on Tuesday.
  • SpaceX shares rose 2.6% to settle at $149.24 on Tuesday.
  • AbbVie shares fell 1.1% to close at $263.29 during the session.
  • AMD shares slipped 0.1% to settle at $607.57.

Anthropic‘s IPO prospectus has revealed the AI developer’s significant reliance on a few tech giants and customers.

About 47% of Anthropic’s sales last year were routed through cloud partners Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet’s Google (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), Reuters reported, citing a confidential IPO filing. These tech behemoths are not only major investors in Anthropic but also its critical suppliers of computing power and direct competitors in AI.

The filing also showed that Anthropic’s revenue is highly concentrated, with two unnamed customers each accounting for 12% of last year’s revenue. The company also warned that major customers could cut or stop spending because many lack long-term contracts. It also acknowledged that relying on a small number of partners and suppliers could create conflicts of interest.

Despite the risks, Anthropic views these relationships as beneficial, stating that it can leverage the vast sales networks of Amazon, Google, and Microsoft Corp.’s (NASDAQ:MSFT) cloud platforms to reach customers and accelerate market penetration.

Anthropic, Google, Amazon and Microsoft did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments

Read Also: OpenAI Targets $30 Billion Mega-Round After Putting IPO Plans on Hold

Claude Usage Drives Anthropic Revenue

Anthropic’s revenue of $3.8 billion came from customers paying based on their usage of the company’s Claude AI system, while subscription revenue amounted to $789 million. The company anticipates consumption-based revenue to constitute “the substantial majority” of its revenue in the future, as per the filing.

Cloud marketplace sales generated roughly $2.16 billion, accounting for 47% of Anthropic’s 2025 annual revenue. By early 2026, its long-term commitments had surpassed $417 billion, covering 3.5 gigawatts of dedicated computing capacity.

Anthropic Faces Losses Despite Rapid Growth

Further details of the prospectus revealed Anthropic’s ambitious plans for AI, despite a net loss of $42 billion in 2025. The company plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Despite revenue surging 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion in 2025, it posted an operating loss of more than $8.06 billion, excluding fundraising-related write-downs.

Despite the risks and losses, tech analyst Dan Ives has called Anthropic’s IPO a watershed event that could benefit the entire technology sector. Ives said an Anthropic IPO could boost the broader tech sector by bringing greater transparency to the AI industry, while noting that investors will expect returns on the heavy upfront spending required for AI and data center infrastructure.

Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares are moving higher in Wednesday’s premarket as investors lean into an improving AI-demand backdrop that could support cloud-compute spending,

The stock was up about 1.75% at $241.50 in premarket trading. Nasdaq futures are down 0.29% while S&P 500 futures have shed 0.12%.

The Catalyst

The latest move comes as AI industry catalysts — including OpenAI’s fast pace of revenue growth and Meta Platforms’ Muse expansion — as supportive for cloud-services demand, with Nebius viewed as having strong exposure to Microsoft and Meta compute spending.

Nebius has also been in focus since Tuesday, when the stock gained nearly 5% as investors returned to high-momentum AI and cloud infrastructure names while watching the company’s pricing power and recent analyst upgrades.

Read Also: MU Stock Split Chatter Divides Traders Online Ahead of Earnings: 'Would It Make Sense' or Get 'Annihilated'?

That same Tuesday coverage also said Nebius was reportedly raising GPU cloud prices by roughly 20% starting Oct. 1, covering several Nvidia GPU models including the H100, H200, B200 and B300.

On the broader tape, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) was down 0.12% in premarket trading, suggesting Nebius’ strength was more stock-specific than sector-driven.

Nebius Performance

Nebius’ past year has been defined by a sharp run-up and a volatile pullback: the stock set its 52-week low at $73.52 on Feb. 5, 2026, then climbed to a 52-week high of $299.86 on June 22, 2026. After that June peak, the stock’s lowest price was $145.80 on July 29, 2026.

Coming into Wednesday, the stock was up 13.47% over about one month through Tuesday’s close, even as it was down 9.11% over about three months. At $240.15, shares were still 19.9% below the June high, placing the stock in a rebound phase off the late-July low rather than back at its peak.

Technical Analysis

NBIS is still in a clear uptrend: at $241.28, it’s trading 7.2% above the 20-day SMA ($224.68) and 45.5% above the 200-day SMA ($165.50), which is the kind of spacing you typically see in momentum-led names. The 20-day SMA is also above the 50-day SMA, and the 50-day SMA is above the 200-day SMA—two bullish crossover signals that keep the longer-term trend pointed higher.

From a structure standpoint, the stock is coming off a recent swing low in July and pushed to a swing high in August, so traders are watching whether this bounce can turn into another leg higher rather than a lower high. The 52-week high was set in June at $299.86, so there’s still overhead room before the stock is back into that prior peak zone.

  • Key Resistance: $254.50 — a nearby ceiling where rebounds can stall, sitting just above the current price and acting like a near-term pivot area
  • Key Support: $204 — a level where buyers previously stepped in, and a meaningful downside reference if the stock starts retracing toward its intermediate trend
